pending_interview.category: System design (ML/AI-specific) — RAG at scale, eval pipeline design, recommendation systems, agent platforms, feature store design
pending_interview.question: You are designing a feature store — a centralized system that stores and serves pre-computed features (inputs) to machine learning models — for a company running 50+ ML models in production across recommendation, fraud detection, and personalization use cases. The models need features served with under 10ms latency online (for real-time inference), and the same features must be available in batch for model training to avoid training/serving skew (the problem where a model is trained on different data than it later sees in production). Walk through your architecture. How do you handle the dual online/offline serving requirement? How do you prevent training/serving skew? How would you design the system to support feature reuse across 50 different models without creating tight coupling or versioning chaos?

REST/GraphQL/gRPC tradeoffs: boundary-based protocol selection and production failure modes.
